_comment: servosity is a SPECIAL case: it is engine-swapped from the servosity-msp mint via a staging strip + de-msp rename ritual that is RE-APPLIED on every reprint, so most of its divergence from a stock print is re-derived, not lost. These entries pin the load-bearing engine-swap invariants so a NAIVE reprint (one that bypassed the ritual) is caught. NOTE: a full reprint-diff would surface more; this records the auth/identity invariants that matter most. Issue #78 (bare SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN lacked the required 'Token ' DRF auth-scheme prefix -> HTTP 403 on every data endpoint) is FIXED in AuthHeader() and pinned below; the servosity-msp engine still emits a bare token, so a reprint that bypassed re-applying this prefix would reintroduce the bug. 2026-08-17 (4.30.3 reprint): the admin-only-endpoints entry gained asserts for two surfaces the 4.24.0 ledger did not cover - cli/internal/cli/channel_workflow.go (the workflow sync resource list) and cli/internal/cli/root_test.go (the 4.30 declared-API-surface conformance test, which FAILS the build if a declared path has no Cobra command). The 4.30.3 reprint reintroduced the endpoints on both and the ledger did not catch them; they are pinned now. secret-echo-decoded-funnel retired 2026-11-03: replaced by the shared credential kit (credkit-wiring), so no entry remains for it.

handfixes.summary: MSP-token auth (SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN env var -> ServosityMspToken -> AuthHeader) is hand-wired by the engine swap
handfixes.why: The servosity-msp engine adds an MSP partner-token auth path the stock print does not have. The env-var wiring and config field are re-applied by the de-msp ritual; a naive reprint that bypassed the ritual would drop them and break authentication.

handfixes.summary: AuthHeader() prepends the DRF 'Token ' scheme to the MSP partner token (issue #78)
handfixes.why: The Servosity API authenticates the MSP partner token via Django REST Framework's TokenAuthentication, which requires the 'Token ' scheme on the Authorization header; a bare value 403s on every data endpoint. The stock servosity-msp engine emits the token verbatim, so the de-msp ritual must re-apply this scheme prefix on every reprint or the bug returns. hasAuthScheme tolerates an already-prefixed value for backward compatibility with the SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN='Token <t>' workaround.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press supports x-prefix on an apiKey header securityScheme (docs/SPEC-EXTENSIONS.md), which would make the press emit the 'Token ' scheme natively and retire this hand-fix. NOT adopted yet: the generated applyAuthFormat path would prepend unconditionally, double-prefixing every user who set SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN='Token <t>' per the old workaround. Adopt only together with a stripAuthScheme-equivalent normalization upstream, and only with a live-tenant retest.

handfixes.summary: issues archived (/issues/archived/) and issues ignored (/issues/ignored/) are stripped from EVERY surface (CLI, MCP code-orch and context, sync, store, workflow resource list, declared-surface conformance test) because they are admin-scoped and 403 for the reseller-scoped partner token this connector ships (PR #178)
handfixes.why: These two GET endpoints are generated from the OpenAPI spec and admin-only; the partner SERVOSITY_MSP_TOKEN gets HTTP 403. A naive reprint regenerates them on every surface (the CLI command files, the MCP code-orch endpoint table agents drive via servosity-msp_search/_execute, the MCP context taxonomy agents use for discovery, the sync resource map + store PK map, the workflow sync resource list, and - since press 4.30 - the declared-API-surface conformance test in root_test.go, which fails the build when a declared path has no Cobra command). The de-msp ritual must re-strip all of them; these not_contains asserts fail CI if any surface reintroduced them. Admin functionality lives in Servosity's separate internal admin CLI (admin-token-scoped) instead. See docs/reprint-survival.md.

handfixes.summary: current-user API-token retrieval is explicit human-only CLI behavior and is excluded from MCP, sync, archive, response caches, and the local search store; schema v10 purges previously mirrored copies (issue #254)
handfixes.why: The generated GET command returned a live credential through every CLI format, MCP code orchestration, default sync, workflow archive, the HTTP response cache, SQLite resources, FTS search, and arbitrary read-only MCP SQL. A reprint would restore all of those generated surfaces. The CLI now requires --reveal-token, forces live/no-cache resolution, and is mcp:hidden. MCP discovery, code orchestration, sync, and archive omit the endpoint. Store schema v10 purges known historical rows and rebuilds FTS before MCP may open an old store, while the generic persistence boundary rejects future sensitive rows. Constructor-time cache cleanup removes the old current-user response namespace for each active cache profile. Logical cleanup cannot erase old binaries, free pages, WAL files, backups, or transcripts, so the security release also requires rotation guidance.

handfixes.summary: auth set-token and auth logout write and delete the credentials store colocated with an explicit --config / SERVOSITY_MSP_CONFIG file, not just the default data-dir store (PR #248)
handfixes.why: The generated cliutil credentials layer is config-path-aware on READ (LoadCredentialsForConfigWithStatus resolves <dir-of-config>/data/credentials.toml and Load prefers it) but not on WRITE: SaveCredentials and RemoveCredentials always resolved the DEFAULT store. With --config or SERVOSITY_MSP_CONFIG set, `auth logout` printed 'Logged out. Credentials cleared.' while the sibling token stayed on disk and kept authenticating every later call, and `auth set-token` wrote the rotated token to the default store while the sibling kept serving the OLD one - a rotation the operator believes happened but did not. The fix adds SaveCredentialsForConfig / RemoveCredentialsForConfig mirroring the read-path resolution, records explicitConfigFile on Config so the write paths can honor it, routes saveCredentialsFirst/ClearTokens through them, and makes the path `auth set-token` prints follow the store it actually wrote. All four files are generated ('DO NOT EDIT'), so a reprint on an unfixed press silently restores the false-logout. Regression tests live in the hand-written cli/internal/config/config_test.go and fail without the fix.

handfixes.summary: the MCP shell-out gate refuses every flag whose usage text names a filesystem location, not just the four names the generated denylist happened to carry (PR #248)
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account, so any forwarded flag that names a local path lets a tool caller choose where that account reads or writes. The generated blockedDestinationFlags list covered audit-dir/o/output/receipt-file and missed --db (every local-store command), --out (qbr, qbr-all), --input (import), --notes-file / --playbook-file / --playbook-notes-file (teach, teach-playbook) and --reconcile (bill): 28 of 155 tools exposed one. Driving learnings_list with {"db": "<any path>"} created a 1.8 MB SQLite file at that path. The fix adds the missing names to the static floor AND adds isFilesystemPathFlag, a per-command rule matching the flag's USAGE text so a newly generated path flag is refused by default. Matching usage rather than name is load-bearing: this CLI ships generated API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values never touch the server filesystem, and a name-based rule would break those real API surfaces. Both files are generated, so a reprint reopens all 28 tools.

handfixes.summary: a host-changing redirect drops EVERY credential-classed header, not only Authorization (PR #248)
handfixes.why: The generated CheckRedirect deleted only Authorization on a cross-host hop while Go replayed every other header verbatim. The 4.30 surface added 26 --x-servosity-mfa flags, so X-Servosity-Mfa is a second live credential on the wire, and config.headers lets an operator put an API key in any header name they like. A 3xx from the API (open redirect or partner handoff) therefore handed those credentials to a host the operator never authenticated against. The fix adds isCredentialHeader (exact names plus a hyphen/underscore SEGMENT match on auth/token/secret/key/session/mfa/otp/signature/... so unrelated names such as X-Assignee do not trip it) and stripCredentialHeaders, called only on the cross-host branch. Same-host redirects still re-derive Authorization, so nonce-bound schemes keep working and paginated redirects do not start 401ing. client.go is generated, so a reprint restores the single-header strip.

handfixes.summary: root.go carries the transcendent Short/Long describing all 13 novel commands, not the press's generic one-liner
handfixes.why: The press emits Short/Long as "Manage servosity-msp resources via the servosity-msp API". That does two kinds of damage at once. It DROPS the discovery surface for every novel command from --help and agent-context - the 13 highlights are the whole reason this connector is more than a generated API wrapper, and an agent reading agent-context can no longer find them. And it prints the internal MINT SLUG servosity-msp where the product name belongs. Note the slug is meaningful, not noise: servosity-msp is the MSP-fleet CLI as distinct from servosity-admin, a separate CLI. The de-msp ritual does not erase that distinction - it renders it in the readable product name, which is why the restored text reads "Servosity Msp CLI - The first MSP-fleet CLI for backup". Do not scrub the MSP distinction; keep the internal slug out of user-facing prose while preserving the product identity. The module path servosity-msp-pp-cli and the SERVOSITY_MSP_* env vars stay untouched by design. Verified dropped by the 4.30.3 reprint; re-apply the transcendent block on every reprint.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For servosity the manifest gained: PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, SERVOSITY_MSP_BASE_URL, SERVOSITY_MSP_RESELLER_ID, SERVOSITY_MSP_USER_AGENT. server.json gained: PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, SERVOSITY_MSP_BASE_URL, SERVOSITY_MSP_RESELLER_ID, SERVOSITY_MSP_USER_AGENT. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, SERVOSITY_MSP_BASE_URL, SERVOSITY_MSP_RESELLER_ID, SERVOSITY_MSP_USER_AGENT. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. 4.34.0 reprint (2026-10-23): the operator levers the press added, SERVOSITY_MSP_MCP_READ_ONLY, SERVOSITY_MSP_NO_LOCAL_DATA and SERVOSITY_MSP_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, are declared on all three channels too; the remote launch line in mcp-install.md does not repeat the HTTP token after the export that mints it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, `analytics` included, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 11 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: companies agents companies-update-latest (POST /companies/{id}/agents/update-latest/); contracts finalize contracts (POST /contracts/{identifier}/finalize/); resellers agents resellers-update-latest (POST /resellers/{id}/agents/update-latest/); restic-backups agent-service-stop restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/agent-service-stop/); restic-backups agent-service-stop-error restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/agent-service-stop-error/); restic-backups restic-interrupt restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/restic-interrupt/); restic-backups restic-migrate restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/restic-migrate/); restic-backups restic-prune restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/restic-prune/); restic-backups restic-repair-index restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/restic-repair-index/); restic-backups restic-repair-snapshots restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/restic-repair-snapshots/); restic-backups start-restore restic-backups (POST /restic-backups/{id}/start-restore/).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: Credential-classed request header values (the X-Servosity-Mfa code on MFA-gated endpoints, any credential-named config.headers entry) are masked in every shown server text like the token, as written and in the single-layer encodings, so an error keeps its status line and message. The shared credential kit withholds whatever a mask misses, in any encoding the contract names, at the output (credkit-wiring).
handfixes.why: The generated maskCredentialText masks only the auth token family. This connector sends a 6-digit MFA code as X-Servosity-Mfa on the encryption-key and restore endpoints and copies operator config.headers onto every request, so an API error that echoed the code printed a live second factor. holdCredentialHeaders records each credential-classed header value the client sends, credentialHeaderSecrets adds config.headers secrets, isCredentialHeader also matches run-together names (X-AuthToken, X-Apikey) through credentialHeaderFragments, and forceEncoded masks the encoded forms of values below minEncodedSecretLen. client.go is generated, so a reprint restores the token-only masks. The bounded short-value decode walk this entry used to pin is replaced by the shared credential kit; internal/credwire/open_classes_leak_test.go TestShortHeldValueInEncodedForms proves the short code in encoded forms on the built binaries.

handfixes.summary: The servosity-msp spec carries an (e.g. <value>) example on every path parameter whose id type the spec fixes, so press 4.34.0 emits a runnable Example on 203 of 291 endpoint commands

The fix is in the library spec (descriptions only; paths, methods and schemas unchanged), so it survives a reprint from that spec by construction. These asserts catch a reprint from an older or vendor spec that drops the examples.

handfixes.summary: Review fixes carried into the hand-written commands at the 4.34.0 reprint: triage mutations from MCP need a bare --confirm, qbr-all is hidden from MCP, freshness readers use the current inventory and keep prior evidence on failed lookups, QBR success rates name an assessed denominator, bill --reconcile is presence-only with null cents, failure-clusters scopes hosts per company and follows next-page links
handfixes.why: Each fix closed a Codex [P1] on the reprint (wrong result an MSP would act on, or a write without confirm). triage ran batch mutations from an MCP tool call with no confirmation; qbr-all wrote one file per company under ./qbrs as the server account; failed freshness lookups erased the prior evidence and stale rows survived inventory changes; QBR success rates counted backups whose quarter could not be assessed; bill --reconcile summed nothing for repeated invoice rows and printed fabricated cents; failure-clusters merged hosts across companies and read only the first page. Tests in the files named below fail without each fix.

handfixes.summary: No credential an API read returns is kept on disk or handed to an MCP agent without a confirm: the store refuses the MFA-secret resources and strips secret-named fields (any casing) from every row, older stores are purged on their first open, secret, non-JSON and secret-endpoint responses are never cached, every MCP tool result has secret fields withheld, and the secret GETs need confirm over MCP
handfixes.why: The api-token containment (issue #254) covered one endpoint. Default sync also mirrored stored credential passwords (GET /credentials/), backup-account MFA codes (/backups/mfa_codes/), the user's MFA backup codes and the MFA-enrollment secret, ShadowProtect product keys, the Postmark API token, agent tokens and the agent provisioning token id into data.db, the typed tables and FTS, where MCP sql and search returned them even with SERVOSITY_MSP_MCP_READ_ONLY=1; the HTTP response cache kept encryption-key and credential reads; and servosity-msp_read returned encryption keys to the agent. The fix: sensitiveMirroredResource refuses backups-mfa-codes, current-user-mfa-backup-codes and current-user-start-mfa (dropped from default sync too, since two of those GETs can regenerate codes or start an enrollment on the server); mergeIncomingResourceData, which every one of the 130 write paths re-decodes before its typed insert, drops persistedSecretFields; stores below schema 13 (every store a released build wrote) are purged on their first read-write open, and read-only opens refuse them until then; writeCacheWithHeaders skips a response carrying a secret field and a one-time sweep deletes cached secret responses; secret_reads.go flips NeedsConfirm on the secret GET endpoints. store.go, client.go and sync.go are generated, so a reprint restores every gap. Round 2 of the publish review found the exact snake_case name list missed the API's PascalCase backup-set passwords (LanPassword, ApplicationSettings.EncryptionPassword), that the mirrored tail tool and plain reads such as resellers.read still returned secrets over MCP, and that INI or env-shaped bodies were cached. Secret fields are now matched by cliutil.IsSecretFieldName on the normalized key; cmd/servosity-mcp's withholdToolSecrets middleware withholds them from every tool result except servosity-msp_execute with confirm: true; the cache skips non-JSON bodies and the secret endpoints by path; sync refuses an explicitly named MFA-secret resource before any request; the purge runs with secure_delete on. Round 3 (adversarial and Codex) found that an oversized tool result is turned into a raw preview string by internal/mcp/bound before the middleware sees it, and that a JSON escape in a key (postmark_server_api_to\u006ben) slipped past the byte prefilter. bound.go's previewEnvelope now withholds secret fields from the whole text before it cuts the preview (a key/value fallback covers text already cut mid-document), JSON nested inside string values is withheld too, and any backslash sends text to the parser.

handfixes.summary: Servosity issue changes as events before Servosity has webhooks: `issues watch` (issues_watch.go) polls every page of the partner issue list read-only, re-reads an active issue that left it to learn archived or ignored, and records servosity.issue.created/updated/archived/ignored/reactivated rows in a vendor_events table (store/vendor_events.go, the zammad connector's table and row shape) beside an issue_watch_state snapshot (store/issue_watch.go), both created from extras.go; `events list` and the read-only MCP tool events_list read it by cursor. recordIssueObservations is the one seam a future signed Servosity webhook receiver calls. Wired by the init hook in issues_watch.go.
handfixes.why: Damien GO 2026-10-27: Servosity has no webhooks yet, so a polling bridge whose store a future issue webhook plugs into (fleet/state/plan-2026-10-27/webhooks.md sections 2 and 4). None of it is in the spec, so a reprint regenerates none of it: every file is hand-written with no DO NOT EDIT marker, wired through the generator's registerNovelCommand hook, and the one edit to a generated file (extras.go migrations) is pinned here. It polls /resellers/{id}/issues/ because partner tokens are refused /issues/, /issues/archived/ and /issues/ignored/ (admin-only, PR #178 and the 2026-05-22 live acceptance), so it never calls the two admin-only lists. That list holds ACTIVE issues only (servosity-api api_v1/views/reseller.py issues), so an active issue that leaves it is re-read with GET /issues/{id}/ and an ignored one is re-read at most hourly (it can still be archived by prune_issues or archive_by_hash); archived is final. handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name: the <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. A store of operator-named text that repeats a held credential is refused by the shared credential kit at each sink: profiles.json, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl (file writes) and the learn tables (its SQL driver), as credkit-wiring pins. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>, then route its sinks through the kit, not its refusal checks.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: --all on a Django REST Framework page-number list follows next until it is null, never asks for the page after the last one, refuses a walk that ends with fewer rows than the envelope's count ({"event":"truncated","fetched":N,"count":M} on stderr and exit 6), and keeps that count in the output as meta.total_count. attention --refresh re-sends every query parameter of the issues next link (page or cursor) and fails rather than counting a partial book. drf_pagination_test.go proves it against a fake DRF server: 27 rows, 10 per page, every listed list command in the JSON and agent shapes, sync plus backup-facts and stale-backups, attention, and the two truncation cases.
handfixes.why: The Servosity API pages lists the DRF way: count, num_pages, next (a full URL or null), previous, results, and 404 {"detail":"Invalid page."} for a page past the last one. Press 4.34.0 generates every list with paginationType page and no next_cursor_path, so paginatedGet followed next to the last page, then its page+1 heuristic asked for one more and the DRF 404 failed the whole --all; an older build (servosity-pp-cli 1.0.0) instead stopped after page 1 with exit 0 and stripped the count, so a caller could not tell rows were missing. attention's own loop followed only a cursor parameter, so a page-number next link ended the walk after page 1. A reprint that drops these edits regresses silently; these asserts and TestDRF* fail.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: infer DRF page-number pagination from a list response schema carrying count, next (uri, nullable) and results, follow next to null, and guard the fetched rows against count. The press's internal spec has next_cursor_path, but this Swagger 2 spec produced next_cursor_path "" on every list, and nothing in a spec expresses the count guard or keeping the count, so this hand-fix stays after any spec annotation.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's earlier credential layer: the funnel, its short-value walk, held_exact, held_persist, held_configured and sent_credentials are gone (retire reason: replaced by the shared credential kit). internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal. credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains and credkit.Exit ends them. Every sink is routed: the client's sends (OutboundGuard around the one Do), feedback, deliver and probe clients through credkit.Transport; the response caches, journal, teach logs, learnings, feedback, export, downloads, QBR output, profiles and AtomicWritePrivateFile through credkit file writes; every SQLite handle through credsql (credkit-sqlite-every-handle); MCP tools through credkit.MCPTools, stdio through MCPIn and MCPOut, HTTP through MCPHTTP (credkit-mcphttp-outermost); the MCP CLI shell-out and the QBR PDF render through credkit.RunCommand; terminal checks through credkit.Terminal. The credentials store and config file are credential sources, listed in Declarations.Files, and are written by AtomicWriteCredentialFile outside the kit as the declared exemption. The kit starts no child with a credential in its argv or environment, so RunCLICommand hands the environment's token to a mirrored tool's child on stdin behind the hidden --credentials-stdin flag (Declarations.StdinFlags); mcpChildEnviron drops the secret variables. Kept outside the kit, by judgment: lock files, the empty SQLite journal file, the .data-db-owner marker and the fingerprint key (constant or random bytes), the journal's torn-tail newline repair, and os.Rename or os.Link of a file the kit just wrote. Vendor secret fields a read returns on purpose (an encryption key, a stored credential's password, an MFA code, --reveal-token) are NOT response fields: secret-family-never-persisted keeps them off disk and away from an MCP agent without a confirm, and holding them would withhold the read a person asked for. The run profile store (profiles.json) is a credential source: loadProfileStore holds every value under a declared credential flag's name (any key case, each duplicate key) before the store is parsed (cliutil.HoldProfileStore, over cliutil.CredentialFlags, which TestCredentialFlagsMatchCliutil keeps equal to Declarations.CredentialFlags); TestProfileCredentialFlagValuesAreHeld drives profile show, use and list.
handfixes.why: Codex round 2 of this branch and the pre-adoption reviews found credential paths the connector's own layer did not close: a held 6-digit MFA code equal to an issue's integer field, an id in another case, short values in encoded forms, values containing a separator, and Cobra parse errors printed before anything was held. internal/credwire/open_classes_leak_test.go builds both binaries and drives each with the reviewer's input; all failed on the pre-adoption head (.review/seen/open-classes-failing-preadopt.log). A reprint regenerates the mains, client.go, store.go and the other generated sink files and drops these routes silently (the build stays green); these asserts and the leak tests fail if it does.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generator should emit the credkit wiring (Start and Exit in each main, credkit.Transport on every client, credkit file writes, the credkit SQLite driver, MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut, MCPHTTP, RunCommand) from a per-connector declarations file, so a reprint keeps it by construction.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves. requireBearerAuthWithLimits is: a preflight that writes nothing (mcpHTTPPreflight: the bearer verdict, and for an authenticated body a bounded, deadline-limited read into memory), then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that writes the refusal (401 with WWW-Authenticate, 413, 408, 400) through the kit's writer, else the MCP handler. A refused request reaches the kit as a clone with no header, trailer or body, so nothing a caller sends without the bearer can mark the kit's acquisition unknown and silence the server; a request expecting 100-continue keeps its body unread for the kit's own 417. The old hijacking rejectMCPHTTPRequest is gone: the kit takes the connection over and closes it.
handfixes.why: Refusals answered outside the kit would carry a piece of a held bearer token that contains their fixed text. internal/credwire/mcphttp_leak_test.go drives each refusal through the real binary and checks a refused request cannot silence the server. main.go is generated; a reprint restores the outer refusals silently.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the inner, kit-wrapped handler and only a write-free preflight runs before credkit.MCPHTTP.

handfixes.summary: servosity-mcp --transport http refuses (403 forbidden origin) a request whose Origin header is present, is not loopback and is not listed in SERVOSITY_MSP_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, before the bearer check; a request with no Origin is accepted. The allowlist is read at startup (loadAllowedHTTPOrigins) and an invalid entry stops the server. The origin parser and allowlist are the current press template's, ported into this engine-swapped main.go.

handfixes.summary: Every read of the connector's config file or credentials store, at startup or later (the MCP server reloads them on every tool call), holds every value in it with credkit.Hold before the file is parsed: config.go's parseConfigData and cliutil's two credentials-store parses first call cliutil.HoldConfigFile (internal/cliutil/credkit_hold.go, hand-written). That is a whole-file tokenizer (no size cutoff; quoted, unterminated and multi-line strings, bare words, inline tables, lines the parser rejects) fed to the kit with its source spellings, then, when the file parses, each decoded leaf. base_url, ca_cert, tls_server_name, token_expiry and client_id (cliutil.NotCredentials) are left unheld when their value is one plain scalar, and base_url still gives up its password and query values; internal/credwire declares exactly those keys as config: Identifiers, and a test keeps the two lists equal.
handfixes.why: The kit's startup capture never sees a file written later. internal/credwire/surfaces_leak_test.go TestMCPConfigReloadHoldsBeforeParse rewrites the file under a running server with a value the TOML parser overflows on and checks its diagnostic never shows it. A reprint regenerates config.go and credentials.go and drops the calls silently.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate a pre-parse hold hook in the config loader, or route every config read through the kit, so runtime reloads are held by construction.

handfixes.summary: store.migrate returns early when the file already carries this schema: PRAGMA user_version equals StoreSchemaVersion and PRAGMA application_id equals migrationStamp, a CRC of the schema version, every migration's text and the parent-key map. The stamp is written last, inside the migration transaction. A reprint or upgrade that changes any of those runs the migrations once; a bare file or an older one runs them as before.
handfixes.why: The press re-runs every idempotent migration on every read-write open: over a thousand statements across this connector's 140 tables. The credential kit checks each one at the SQL sink, which took a store-touching command from 0.18 s to 12 to 15 s and every fresh-store unit test past the package's 10-minute timeout. With the stamp the same command takes 0.5 s after its first run. Kit note: .review/kit-findings.md records the per-statement cost. store.go is generated; a reprint drops this silently and these asserts fail.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: skip the idempotent migration pass when a schema fingerprint on the file matches, for every connector; the cost is a fixed one on each open even before the kit.

The press generates every GET as a sync resource when its response has no schema. client.go and sync.go are regenerated by a reprint, so the resource comes back and the guard goes; these asserts and TestPlainSyncSkipsBinaryResources (built binary, held token) fail.

handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 generates each list with a default page size of 0, so --all sent no page_size and the server paged 10 rows at a time. The value goes on the wire only: paginatedGet's pageSize stays 0, so the server's next link still ends the walk and a server capping below 100 loses no rows. A reprint regenerates helpers.go and drops it; TestAllSendsDefaultPageSize fails.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored and sync keeps walking, then ends that resource failed with the row ids
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named in a sync_error event and in the resource's error, the run exits non-zero, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows).

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.
